$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 2 of N, 2026-11-22 (REG-357, owner: do only 20% of the remaining cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. The batch is every 5th keyword still without a reason, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object) so simple and complex ones are mixed. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.concept.softDelete: A record deleted by mistake must be recoverable and its history intact, yet hidden from every list and report; flipping a platform-managed deleted-at marker once, in the generated reads and writes, is the only way that holds on every screen without each query remembering a filter.
reasons.field.id: Every record needs one stable identifier the platform can key reads, links and events on; naming it explicitly lets the model say which box it is instead of the generator guessing from a naming habit.
reasons.flowStep.parallelAwait: An approval that needs three managers should not wait for them one after another; a loop that parks every iteration's wait at once is the only way to do that durably, and a sequential loop plus an expression cannot park in parallel.
reasons.index.unique: 'One price per product and day' must hold even when two screens or an import race each other; only the database can refuse the repeat atomically, and a validation expression in a flow would let both writes through.
reasons.presentationMetadata.listColumn: A list that shows all forty boxes is unreadable; a per-box switch for 'is this a column' trims it without declaring a separate list screen for every concept.
reasons.queryParameter.required: A query like 'orders of a city' is meaningless with the city missing; declaring the blank mandatory makes the caller fail early with a clear error instead of returning every row.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.layout: Some lists read better as cards than as a table; a two-value choice on the generated surface picks it without a hand-made page, and the default keeps the common case free of declaration.
reasons.domainType.baseType: A domain type such as 'postal code' has to be stored as something; the base type gives every box that uses it the same storage without repeating the type on each field.
reasons.field.type: Every box holds a kind of value, and storage, validation, the form control and the API all derive from it; a fixed menu of types is the smallest vocabulary that lets one declaration drive all four.
reasons.httpConnectorAuth.type: Outside services ask for different logins (none, bearer, basic, a key in a header or in the address); a closed list of schemes lets the platform build the header itself so no author hand-writes request signing.
reasons.panelAction.operation: A button tied to a concept can read, add, change or remove a row; a choice of four verbs reuses the generated mutations and their permission checks instead of a flow per button.
reasons.panelWidget.kind: A wall-board mixes a number, a chart, an action bar, a history and a table; a closed list of widget kinds is how the page says which of the built-in pieces to draw without hand-written UI code.
reasons.regionMount.render: A region is normally drawn by the platform, sometimes by a component the app's developers wrote and sometimes as a paintable board; a three-way choice marks where hand-written code takes over, with the generated rendering as the default.
reasons.agentAccessExposure.roles: Only managers should be offered the refund tool in a chat; filtering the offer by role keeps the tool list short for everyone else, while the app's own permissions still check every call.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.columns: A generated list must say which boxes it shows and in which order; naming them is shorter than a custom screen and keeps the list consistent with the concept when a box is renamed.
reasons.capabilityOperation.errors: A flow can only react differently to 'card refused' and 'service down' if the operation names its failures and classifies them; without the list every failure looks the same and retries become blind.
reasons.conversion.claims: A hand-written Java conversion is a black box, so the platform cannot know which boxes it settles; declaring them lets the checker verify they exist and that nothing else is left unconverted.
reasons.externalAi.prompts: A flow that asks an outside AI for text needs a named request with a vendor and the shape of the answer; checking the answer against that shape before the flow sees it keeps free-form model output from leaking into records.
reasons.flowHook.steps: A hook that inserts behaviour into another flow is useless without the steps it inserts; the list is the payload, and at least one is required so an empty hook is an error, not a silent no-op.
reasons.flowStep.steps: A loop needs a body; the body is ordinary flow steps run once per item, so the same step vocabulary serves inside and outside the loop and no second language is needed.
reasons.index.fields: An index is the ordered list of boxes it covers; the order matters because the database can use only a leading prefix for lookups, so it cannot be inferred from a set.
reasons.pack:concepts: A pack is only useful if it brings record kinds with it; listing them here lets apps refer to them as 'pack::Concept' so two packs never collide on a name.
reasons.pack:fragments: A big pack gets unwieldy in one file; fragments let it be split into local files merged at load, with no change to how consumers see it. Keeping this key is cheap, but no official pack needs it yet.
reasons.pack:queries: A pack that brings records usually also brings the questions people ask of them, such as 'which orders are late'; shipping them with the pack saves every consuming app from rewriting the same query.
reasons.panelDataSource.addFormFields: The form that adds a row to a table should ask for item and quantity and nothing else; a short list of boxes avoids showing the whole concept in a small dialog.
reasons.property.settableAt: A setting such as the free-shipping limit may differ by branch but not by single user; listing the levels where a value may be set stops anyone from overriding it at a level the business did not intend.
reasons.query.parameters: A query that leaves a blank, such as the city, must say which blanks exist and their types so callers bind them by name and the generated API and forms can validate them.
reasons.root:capabilities: An app deals with the outside world in two directions, calling services and receiving notices; one declared list of those dealings is the single place to see, secure and audit every outside contact.
reasons.root:fieldConventions: Any box ending in 'Dt' being a date should be said once, not on every field; naming rules keep large models short, and the platform's own rules apply when the model says nothing.
reasons.root:queries: 'Orders of this city, newest first' is asked again and again; naming the question once lets screens, flows and the API share it instead of each re-writing the filter.
reasons.schemaObject.required: A structure without its city is useless; listing the parts that must be present refuses a half-filled value at the door, which a bare type cannot express.
reasons.capabilityPolicy.retryCount: A call to the carrier fails now and then for no reason; a bounded retry count absorbs those blips without a flow loop and, with an idempotency key, without doing the work twice.
reasons.field.max: Nobody can sell minus five or give 500 percent discount; an inclusive upper bound is enforced by the database, the API and the form together, so no screen can forget it.
reasons.field.precision: A money amount has a fixed number of digits; stating the total digits makes the database column and the form agree and stops a stray extra zero from becoming a million.
reasons.httpConnector.maxRetries: A request that reads a parcel's status fails sometimes and is safe to repeat; a small capped retry count, limited to methods that are safe to repeat, makes the call reliable without any code.
reasons.presentationMetadata.order: People fill a form in a natural sequence, not in the order the boxes were declared; an explicit position per box is the only way to say it without reordering the concept itself.
reasons.schemaObject.minItems: A structure that holds a list may need at least one element, such as one contact; a lower bound refuses the empty list, which the type alone would accept.
reasons.agentAccess.channels: The shop may want the helper on Telegram but not yet on WhatsApp; a switch per channel, all closed until opened, keeps the doors the owner chose and no others.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.bandPickers: A clerk adds receipt lines by choosing products in a pop-up; one picker per band keeps that pop-up declarative, with a ready-made selection panel or just a filter, instead of a hand-made dialog.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.uiState: A 'show details' toggle changes only how a page looks and must never be saved with the record; a declared, named, transient state lets conditions read it without polluting the commit.
reasons.capabilityOperation.input: An operation like 'charge' needs an amount and a card token; stating the input type lets the checker reject a wrong call before it leaves the app, by reference or inline.
reasons.concept.access: In a clinic, each doctor should open only their own patients; a rule that lives with the data holds on every screen, flow and API, where a per-screen check would leak through the one screen that forgot it.
reasons.conversion.javaHook: When no ready-made conversion operation fits, a developer writes it in Java; running it in the isolated plugin pool with the usual safety checks is the last rung before changing the platform. Whether it stays follows the hand-written-code decision.
reasons.externalAi.limits: An outside AI is billed per use and a runaway flow can burn the month's budget; limits naming declared settings cap calls and cost per axis, and can be tuned per branch without editing the model.
reasons.field.reference: An order must point at a customer instead of copying the customer's data into every order; a declared reference keeps the link valid, lets the database enforce it and gives the form a picker.
reasons.flow.outputSchema: A flow that returns a quote must say what comes back, so callers and the checker know the shape without running it; the type is the contract between a flow and its callers.
reasons.flowStep.policy: Calling the payment service may need more retries and a longer timeout than the default, only at this step; a per-step override avoids declaring a second operation just to change resilience.
reasons.httpConnector.auth: The carrier's website lets in only those who show a key; naming the scheme once on the connector gives every operation the same authentication, with no login by default.
reasons.httpConnectorOperation.response: A carrier's answer has dozens of fields and the app needs one; a pointer into the response returns just that part, so no map step has to dig it out afterwards.
reasons.lifecycleState.metadata: An author sometimes wants a note on a stage, such as 'billing starts here', that tools and humans can read; a free notebook carried unchanged adds no behaviour, so no new keyword is needed for each such note.
reasons.pack:metadata: A publisher wants to say 'tested with app version 4' on the pack; a free notebook carried unchanged serves that without adding a keyword for every kind of note.
reasons.panelAction.metadata: Whoever adds a button may want a note beside it, such as who asked for it; a free notebook carried unchanged does that without a new keyword, and the platform acts on none of it.
reasons.property.label: The administration page should show 'Free shipping limit', not a technical name, in the person's language; a localisable label is the only place that text can live without code.
reasons.root:agentAccess: A company wants its AI assistants to read orders but never delete anything; one place that says what agents are offered and on which channels is the audit point for everything an agent can do.
reasons.seed.data: Sample records make a fresh app usable at once; writing them like a request to the app, with references to other samples and generated values, avoids a hand-written loader and typing every row.
reasons.workbenchBandPicker.label: The button that opens a product pop-up needs a caption such as 'Add products'; a localisable label keeps it in the person's language, and an absent one would show a technical name.
reasons.agentAccessExposure.aggregate: An assistant should read a whole order, header and lines, and save it in one go; exposing the aggregate whole goes through the same commit the workbench uses, so rules apply and a half-saved order is impossible.
reasons.aggregateBalance.leftValue: A balance rule compares the rows marked as one side, say 'Origem', with the rows of the other; it has to be told that marker, and no expression can pick it because the rule runs inside the commit.
reasons.aggregateCollection.concept: A document is more than its header: an invoice has lines. Naming the kind of record the lines are is how the document becomes one whole that is read and saved together.
reasons.aggregateCollectionLookupField.valueFiel: A saved question answers with several columns but a line needs just one, such as the quantity on hand; naming the column attaches exactly that without a join written by hand.
reasons.appShellNavItem.label: A menu entry should read 'Customers', not the technical name of a concept; a localisable label is the only place that wording can live.
reasons.autoPanelDataSource.procedure: A list of 'best customers' is worked out, not stored, so no generated query gives it; naming a flow as the row source is the escape rung. The keyword keeps its old name 'procedure', but since REG-342 the name must resolve to a declared flow.
reasons.capability.uid: Renaming 'Payments' to 'Billing' must not look like one capability vanishing and another appearing; a stable identity made once lets the platform recognise the rename. It is optional and exists only for the migration tool.
reasons.capabilityPolicy.idempotencyKeyField: A customer double-clicks 'Pay' and the card is charged twice; naming the input box that identifies the request lets the platform recognise the repeat, which a retry count alone cannot.
reasons.concept.module: A big app has a sales area and a warehouse area that both say 'Customer' and mean different things; assigning a concept to a module gives each its own namespace, so a name needs no ugly prefix.
reasons.conceptAccess.read: Each salesperson should see their own customers; a one-line condition checked for every record, with the asker's identity available, makes other rows invisible on every screen and API without writing per-screen filters.
reasons.conversion.set: After finding the city by its name, the customer must keep the city's id; naming the box that receives the matched id is what makes a lookup conversion a real change and not just a search.
reasons.conversionLookupMatch.on: A lookup compares a box of the other concept with a box of this one; naming the other side's box completes the pair, and no expression is needed.
reasons.documentLogo.field: A printed document needs the company's logo, which is stored as a picture on its record; naming that box lets the document pull it in without a hand-written template.
reasons.enumOption.icon: A small truck beside 'Shipped' makes a long list readable at a glance; a named icon per choice gives that without custom rendering code.
reasons.eventPayloadField.name: An event carries named pieces of data, such as the order id, and subscribers read them by name; the name is the contract between whoever raises the event and whoever listens.
reasons.field.itemIdentityField: In a list of order items two entries are 'the same' when their product code matches; naming that box is the only way to give duplicate detection a meaning, together with the duplication policy.
reasons.flow.description: Six months later a colleague, or an AI helper, opens 'Close month' and needs to know what it is for; a sentence on the flow is the cheapest documentation that cannot drift apart from it.
reasons.flowStep.actionName: The platform already generates an action per concept and a flow may want to run one; naming it reuses the generated rule and permissions instead of re-writing them as steps.
reasons.flowStep.errorTarget: The e-mail service is down and the whole flow should not die because of it; storing the failure under a name and letting the step succeed lets a later step decide, which a global error handler cannot do per call.
reasons.flowStep.itemKey: Each turn of a loop needs a name for the item being handled; without it the body could not refer to the current customer, and the expression language has no implicit loop variable.
reasons.flowStep.to: A notify step has to know who gets the message, a fixed address or one taken from the flow's data; this is the only recipient field, and notifying reuses the platform's own notification ability so nothing else is declared.
reasons.guidePageGadget.title: A big number alone means little; a heading such as 'Orders waiting' says what it is counting, and it is localisable like any other text a person reads.
reasons.guidePageTheme.logoText: A small company has no logo picture, only its name; text shown in the place of a logo is the lightest way to brand a guide page without hosting an image.
reasons.httpConnectorAuth.secretEnvVar: A password must never be written in the model, because the model is shared and stored; naming the machine's environment variable that holds it keeps the secret out of the file and out of version control.
reasons.humanTask.title: An approver's inbox lists many tasks and each needs a clear heading such as 'Approve purchase PO-1042'; placeholders filled from the flow's data make the heading specific without code.
reasons.invariant.name: When a record breaks a rule the message must say which one; a name is also how another concept replaces the rule, so it cannot be left to an index in a list.
reasons.lifecycleTransition.to: A move ends in a stage; together with where it starts, the destination defines one allowed step, and the closed set of steps is what makes illegal jumps impossible.
reasons.pack:dslVersion: The language changes over time; a pack must say which version it was written in so the loader can refuse one it cannot read instead of misreading it.
reasons.packRef.from: A pack lives in a registry or a git repository and the model must say where to fetch it and at which version; one remote address, kept apart from a local file reference by design, is the whole contract.
reasons.panelAction.flow: A 'Reopen ticket' button has several steps to run; naming the flow lets a button start the recipe with its durability and permissions, instead of copying the steps into the page.
reasons.panelDataSource.name: A panel can have several lists, say orders and order lines; each needs a name that bindings, widgets and row buttons refer to, because position in a list would break when one is added.
reasons.panelDataSource.totalField: Under a table of order lines a footer should show the total; naming the numeric box to add up gives a display total without a query or an aggregate, at the price of being worked out in the browser only.
reasons.panelSlot.component: An app's developers wrote their own little drawing and registered it in a file; naming it here is how the page learns which of their pieces goes into the reserved place, which is the extension point for hand-written screens.
reasons.presentationMetadata.currency: A price of 1500 means little until the screen shows 'R$ 1.500,00'; a currency code lets the field be formatted as money everywhere with the right symbol and separators.
reasons.presentationMetadata.group: In a customer form the phone and e-mail belong together under 'Contact'; a group name clusters boxes under one heading without a custom form layout.
reasons.presentationMetadata.tab: A big record such as an employee is easier to use split into tabs; naming the tab per box does that without a hand-made form.
reasons.propertyScope.name: A level of the setting cascade, such as 'branch', needs a name that the settings point to; the name is the handle that settable-at and values use to say where a value applies.
reasons.queryComputedColumn.name: A computed column such as 'to buy', needed minus owned, needs its own heading to be read and sorted on; the name is how the answer and the screen refer to it.
reasons.queryParameter.name: Whoever runs a query must say which city and which month; the name is how callers bind each blank and how the query refers to it, so order of arguments never matters.
reasons.referenceDefinition.target: A reference must say which kind of record it points at; the target name, plain or qualified by pack or module, is what lets the database keep the link valid and the form offer a picker.
reasons.root:namespace: The generated app needs a home name for its code and a prefix for its identifiers; it is required and has no sensible default, because two apps with the same name would clash.
reasons.schemaObject.description: A sentence saying what a part of a structure means, such as 'street and number, without the city', is what lets a person or an AI filling it in know what belongs there.
reasons.sequence.format: Invoices read 'INV-2026-0001', not 17; a template with a padded counter and optional date parts, restarting when the date part changes, is something no expression can do because it needs the allocator's state.
reasons.transactionHooks.onLoad: When a receipt opens, some values should be filled from the purchase order; a flow run once before the first draw returns the starting draft. The keyword says 'procedure' in its older wording, but since REG-342 it names a flow.
reasons.workbenchActionApplyTo.collection: When 'Suggest location' answers, the new row must go into the right list of the draft, such as the receipt's lines; naming the collection is the destination of that appended row.
